finding.claim: SSRF via a broken host allowlist. The check uses host.endswith("example.com"). It has no leading dot and ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined but never used. Any domain ending in the string, such as attackerexample.com, passes. The attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at an internal address (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, or RFC1918 ranges), so the server fetches internal services. The response length is returned (len(r.text)), which gives a blind oracle for internal resources. No resolved-IP validation is done.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
suffix check without a dot boundary; evilexample.com passes
request is sent to the attacker-controlled URL

finding.guards_checked: Only the endswith("example.com") hostname check exists. There is no dot boundary, no scheme restriction, no resolved-IP or private-range block, and no authentication. ALLOWED_SUFFIX is unused. httpx does not follow redirects by default (follow_redirects=False), so redirect-based bypass is not the vector here. The /ping route uses a constant URL and is SAFE.

verdict.guard_found: Only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (no dot boundary, a suffix check that does not close the finding); ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused; no auth, scheme or resolved-IP checks.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11-16 takes the unauthenticated `url` query param, and the only guard at mirror.py:13 is a dot-less endswith, so attackerexample.com passes and reaches httpx get at mirror.py:16, with len(r.text) returned at mirror.py:17.
